$description: Shopify's content guidelines for merchant-facing experiences. Confident, empowering, action-oriented — written for people running a business.

voice.identity: A trusted advisor who has seen thousands of merchants build businesses — helpful, specific, never preachy.

attributes.name: Empowering
attributes.description: Merchants are capable adults. Give them information and tools, not a tutorial. Respect their expertise in their own business.

attributes.name: Confident
attributes.description: Say things directly. 'This will take 5 minutes' — not 'This may take approximately a few minutes.'

attributes.name: Action-oriented
attributes.description: Every screen answers: what can the merchant do here, and what's the outcome? Lead with action, not description.

attributes.name: Practical
attributes.description: Concrete over abstract. 'Your customers will see this as the sender name' — not 'This impacts brand perception.'

attributes.name: Inclusive by default
attributes.description: Merchants sell worldwide — write for global commerce, not US retail.

tone_shifts.onboarding: Welcoming but fast. Don't slow experienced sellers down. Offer guidance, don't impose it.
tone_shifts.errors: Specific about what happened, specific about the fix. Acknowledge that merchant time is money.
tone_shifts.settings: Neutral and clear. Explain what each option does in merchant terms, not engineering terms.
tone_shifts.success: Celebrate what matters — first sale, milestones. Don't inflate small actions.
tone_shifts.help: Scannable. Lead with the answer. Put the explanation after.

use: customer (not consumer or user, in merchant-facing context)
product (not SKU, item, unit — unless precision matters)
learn more (for links to longer guidance)
turn on / turn off (not enable / disable)
avoid: journey (customer journey is OK; everything else is a path)
never: Gendered assumptions about who runs a business

grammar.voice: Active voice. 'Add a product' — not 'A product can be added.'
grammar.contractions: Use them. They're natural and save space.
grammar.titles: Sentence case for headings, buttons, page titles.
grammar.numbers: Numerals for most numeric contexts — merchants read dashboards full of numbers. Spell out one through nine only in pure prose.
grammar.currency: Always use the merchant's configured currency. Never assume USD. Format by locale.
grammar.dates: Use localized formats. Default to unambiguous: 'January 5, 2026' or '5 January 2026' depending on locale.

errors.structure: What the merchant was trying to do → why it didn't work → what to do now.
errors.example-good: We couldn't publish this product. Add a title and at least one variant, then try again.
errors.example-bad: Product save failed. Check your input.

empty-states.structure: What this section is for in the merchant's business → the one action that starts it.
empty-states.example-good: Your customers will appear here once they place their first order. Import existing customers to get started.

rules: Match the action to the outcome — the button's label is a promise.
Don't use 'Submit' — say what gets submitted.
Lead with what matters to the merchant.
No clever wordplay — this is a tool, not a brochure.
Question format is fine when the heading maps to a decision the merchant is making.
Global by default — don't assume US retail, US sizing, US currency.
Describe businesses neutrally: 'your business' works for a solo seller or a 500-person team.
Use 'staff' or 'team' not 'employees' (contractors, family members, partners may be involved).
No assumption of physical retail or online-only — Shopify merchants run both.
